practice.foundation[1]: The solution treats membership of one minimum cut as sufficient. Another minimum cut could remain unchanged when either proposed edge is upgraded; supply enough network or cut information to establish a successful upgrade.

practice.development[2]: The stated minimum cut is incorrect: $\{SB,AC\}$ has capacity $20+18=38$. Widening $BC$ or $BD$ leaves this cut unchanged. Correct the givens and solution.

practice.mastery[1]: Establish which competing cuts contain the upgraded pipes and that no omitted cut changes the answer. The solution assumes both other cuts stay unchanged.

practice.mastery[2]: Slack in the original flow does not guarantee slack in a maximum flow after the other reduction. Supply a network or sufficient joint cut information to determine the simultaneous result.
quiz.q1: The arithmetic and distractors are consistent, but this supplied-flow shortfall type is not asked in the booklet.
quiz.q3: No single option is determined. Specify that $C_2$ excludes the upgraded edge; otherwise option 1 can also be correct and its explanation is not necessarily a mistake.
quiz.q4: Specify that the utilised flow is from a maximum-flow assignment. Without this condition, unchanged maximum flow is not established and numerical decreases cannot all be dismissed.

quiz.q9: Supplied-flow surplus calculation is not asked in the booklet. The $120$ distractor also needs a specific mistake that actually produces that value.

theory: Reducing an edge below its utilised flow need not decrease maximum flow because flow may be rerouted. Increasing an edge on one minimum cut is necessary but not sufficient when other minimum cuts remain unchanged; upgrades must account for every restrictive cut and for edges shared between cuts. Distinguish an arbitrary current flow from a maximum-flow assignment when using unused edge capacity to assess a reduction.
